statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

domain_restrictions: n, k, and l are integers
the quotient is only assumed to have meaning as a polynomial when it simplifies to one in q
the phrase has only nonnegative coefficients refers to the standard expansion as a polynomial in q
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer triple n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the ratio of the Gaussian binomial coefficient for n choose k to the one for n choose l is actually a polynomial in q, then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative.
quantifier_order: for every integer k satisfying 0 <= k <= n
for every integer l satisfying 0 <= l <= n
if the quotient of the two Gaussian binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q, then its coefficients are all nonnegative

variables.domain: all integers, effectively nonnegative because k and l are between 0 and n
variables.name: n
variables.role: upper parameter of the Gaussian binomial coefficients

variables.name: k
variables.role: lower index in the numerator Gaussian binomial coefficient

variables.name: l
variables.role: lower index in the denominator Gaussian binomial coefficient

variables.name: q
variables.role: base and expansion variable for the Gaussian binomial coefficients

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses appear in the statement
